subject: zoology_2
question_text: Describe various types of barriers of innate immunity.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.37, SAQ 31. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Physical barriers
steps.why: The cheapest defence is to keep the germ out altogether, which is what an unbroken surface does.
common_mistakes: Naming antibodies. Innate immunity is not antibody based.
steps.memory_tip: Skin keeps them out; mucus traps the ones that get in.
steps.margin_note: Name all four barriers first, then explain each.
lines: Innate immunity is the inborn resistance
to disease. It works through four barriers:
Skin prevents the entry of micro organisms.
Mucus membranes trap and kill micro

steps.label: Physiological barriers
steps.why: Body fluids are made hostile to germs, so anything that gets past the surface meets acid or an enzyme.
common_mistakes: Calling saliva a physical barrier. It is a secretion, so it is physiological.
steps.memory_tip: Acid in the stomach, lysozyme in tears and saliva.
steps.margin_note: Name the secretions and what is in them.

steps.label: Cellular barriers
steps.why: Some white cells patrol the body and swallow anything foreign, without waiting to be told which germ it is.
common_mistakes: Naming B cells or T cells. Those belong to acquired immunity.
Leaving out what these cells do.
steps.memory_tip: These cells eat the germ instead of marking it.

steps.label: Cytokine barriers
steps.why: An infected cell warns its neighbours, so the cells around it are already defended before the virus reaches them.
common_mistakes: Writing that cytokines kill the virus directly. They protect the cells not yet infected.
steps.memory_tip: The infected cell shouts a warning to the cells around it.

insider_note: Four barriers, four marks — one each. Name all four in the opening line so none is forgotten, then take them in order.
